scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8044: We are in Campus 1 -- the PC5-PC14 machines. Since
some point today we cannot reach anything over in Campus 2 (the 10.5.x and
10.6.x computers); it all just times out from here. Everything inside our
own campus is fine, so the break is between the campuses -- on your side,
not ours. It went like this once before, too. I cannot tell you what was
done about it back then, but that is your record to check, not mine. Get
us reconnected to Campus 2 today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16's ospfd is running, the mswitch0
  <-> router16 adjacency is Full, Campus 1 prefixes are advertised, and PC5
  reaches Campus 2 (e.g. 10.5.0.1) with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an edge/routing outage
  that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Campus 1 cut off from
Campus 2 / the backbone -- is NOT reproducible: router16's ospfd is running
(`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), its OSPF adjacency to mswitch0 is Full, and PC5 reaches
10.5.0.1 (Campus 2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Campus 1 edge is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC5 -> Campus 2), finds it working, checks router16's ospfd and the OSPF
adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or a broken
edge to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router16/mswitch0 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough end-to-end investigation found no fault anywhere in the inter-campus path. The complete data-plane test matrix — pc5 (172.16.10.5/VLAN 10), pc9 (172.16.20.9/VLAN 20), and pc12 (172.16.30.12/VLAN 30) in Campus 1 all successfully pinged pc1 (10.5.0.1/VLAN 5) and pc3/pc4 (10.6.0.3-4/VLAN 6) in Campus 2, and the reverse direction (pc3 → all three Campus 1 VLANs) was equally clean — 0% packet loss on every pair tested.

The control plane is equally healthy. OSPF is fully converged across all participating devices: mswitch0 peers with router16; router16 peers with router7; router7 maintains Full adjacencies with router1, router10, router8, and router16; router8 peers with router7 and router17; router17 peers with router11, router10, router8, and sshswitch. Every router's RIB contains the correct routes for both 10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24 (Campus 2) and 172.16.10/20/30.0/24 (Campus 1). The OSPF configurations on sshswitch and mswitch0 correctly advertise their local VLAN subnets into area 0.

No access-control lists, iptables rules, rp_filter restrictions, or interface errors were found on any transit device. IP forwarding is enabled everywhere it needs to be.

Root cause: There is no fault. The network is operating correctly.

Corrective action: None required. The ticket premise — that Campus 1 cannot reach Campus 2 — does not reflect the current state of the lab. The helpdesk should re-verify connectivity from the user's endpoint; the infrastructure side is fully operational.
